question: When three parallel lines are cut by two transversals and the intercepts made by the first transversal are in the ratio 3 : 5, then the intercepts made by the second transversal are in the ratio ____
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the **Intercept Theorem** (also known as Thales' Theorem for parallel lines), the ratio of **intercepts** made by any transversal on a set of **parallel lines** is always **constant**.

If the first transversal makes intercepts in the ratio 3 : 5, every other transversal will also make intercepts in the same ratio 3 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three **parallel lines** (say l₁, l₂, l₃) and two **transversals** (say t₁ and t₂). The intercepts made by t₁ are in ratio 3 : 5.

**Formula Used:** If three or more **parallel lines** are cut by two **transversals**, then the segments intercepted on the transversals are **proportional**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed2381b427577ebb1eda5e893e1ab549c53a14b41deff5c184c6dcebe9390099.png] 

⇒ Let the intercepts on the first transversal be **A** and **B**. Ratio A : B = 3 : 5.

⇒ Let the corresponding intercepts on the second transversal be **C** and **D**.

⇒ According to the **proportionality theorem**: A ÷ B = C ÷ D

⇒ 3 ÷ 5 = C ÷ D

⇒ C : D = 3 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Intercept Theorem

If three or more **parallel lines** intersect two transversals, then they cut off the transversals in **proportional segments**.

Midpoint Theorem

A special case of this theorem where the ratio is **1 : 1**, implying the **parallel line** passes through the **midpoints** of the transversal segments.

Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT)

Also known as **Thales's Theorem**, it states that if a line is drawn **parallel** to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides, the other two sides are divided in the same **ratio**.</p
